newsitem.title: UK: Lloyd's announces changes to '97 capacity auctions.
newsitem.headline: Lloyd's announces changes to '97 capacity auctions.

text.p: Lloyd's of London on Monday announced changes to the 1997 syndicate capacity auctions, designed to increase price stability and the efficiency of the process.

There have been criticism of previous auctions which allow members to buy and sell participations in insurance syndicates for the next year, that bidders have been making inflated bids in order to guarantee success but then have only to pay a common 'strike price'.
In this year's auction those succesful in acquiring capacity will instead pay what they bid.
All those surrendering capacity will receive the same premium.
Stricter surveillance of the auctions will also be in place following worries about insider dealing.
This year's will be conducted on a fully electronic system which will allow a closer eye to be kept on the auction process.
Lloyd's said that it would investigate any examples of insider trading it found and would be extending checks to 'connected' persons during the auctions.

The insurance market is still investigating a 'handful' of cases from last year when some 1.4 billion pounds ($2.3 billion) of capacity - 14 percent of the market's total - was allocated at a value of 35 million pounds.
The 1997 auctions will begin on July 8 and end on September 24 with a total of eight auctions being held. Each auction will run for two days.
A limited auction of capacity released by members who die late in the year will be held in December. ($ = 0.612 British Pounds)
